metadata.question: Did the burned area north and west of Pacific Palisades, California increase between January 6, 2025 and January 14, 2025?

data.raw_code: 1. Search strategy (Collection, Date, Location): - MODIS Burned Area (MCD64A1) provides per-pixel monthly burn masks. The next best option is the FireCCI51 (monthly) or the “MODIS Burned Monthly” (also monthly). FireCCI51 is updated faster in GEE so we try it first. - Dates: two calendar months – January 2025 (1 Jan – 31 Jan 2025) and, since 14 Jan is still inside January, we need an earlier reference. The question wants the interval 6–14 Jan 2025. Monthly product cannot slice a 8-day window, but we can answer “increase inside the same calendar month” by taking the cumulative burn prior to 6 Jan and compare it with the cumulative burn through 14 Jan (both inside January 2025). - If still the collection is empty, try MODIS Burned Area Monthly or even Sent.2 hotspot bands, but fire products are usually the most reliable and fast-updated. 2. Masking strategy: - FireCCI51 already has a QA band (BurnDate). We keep only pixels where BurnDate ≠ 0 to indicate burned pixels. 3. Logic to distinguish Valid Zero (A/B) from Null/Error (C3): - Compute number of burned pixels for two time spans: • pre6 – images whose time_start ≤ 2025-01-05 (so all burns before 6 Jan) • thru14 – images whose time_start ≤ 2025-01-14 (so all burns through 14 Jan) - take the difference: burned_area_14 – burned_area_6. - If either collection is empty (size 0) → C1. - If all valid pixels are 0 after masking (counts 0) → C2. - If diff is None/NaN → C3. - If diff > 0 → burned area increased, answer A. - Else (diff == 0 or <0) answer B. ```python import ee ee.Initialize(project='earthsense-436113') # 1. Geometry (Pacific Palisades polygon – north-west suburbs) palisades = ee.Geometry.Polygon([ [-118.56,34.08],[-118.52,34.08],[-118.52,34.04],[-118.56,34.04] ]) # 2. Collection choice fire = ee.ImageCollection('ESA/CCI/FireCCI/51/v1'). \ filter(ee.Filter.date('2025-01-01','2025-01-31')). \ filterBounds(palisades) # safety 1 – any data at all? if fire.size().getInfo() == 0: print('No fire imagery for Jan 2025.') print('C1') exit() # 3. cumulative burned area snapshots pre6 = fire.filterDate('2025-01-01','2025-01-06') thru14= fire.filterDate('2025-01-01','2025-01-15') def burnedPixels(col,name): if col.size().getInfo()==0: print(f'{name}: No images'); return 0 comp = col.select('BurnDate').toBands() mask = comp.gt(0) # 0 means unburned count = mask.selfMask().reduceRegion( reducer=ee.Reducer.count(), geometry=palisades, scale=1000, maxPixels=1e9).values().getInfo() return sum(count) if count else 0 burn6 = burnedPixels(pre6,'pre6') burn14 = burnedPixels(thru14,'thru14') # safety 2 – no valid pixels if burn6+burn14==0: print('No valid burn pixels.') print('C2') exit() print(f'Burned pixels total: before6={burn6} through14={burn14}') if burn14 > burn6: print('A') else: print('B') ```
data.code:
import ee
ee.Initialize(project='earthsense-436113')

# 1. Geometry (Pacific Palisades polygon – north-west suburbs)
palisades = ee.Geometry.Polygon([
    [-118.56,34.08],[-118.52,34.08],[-118.52,34.04],[-118.56,34.04]
])

# 2. Collection choice
fire = ee.ImageCollection('ESA/CCI/FireCCI/51/v1'). \
        filter(ee.Filter.date('2025-01-01','2025-01-31')). \
        filterBounds(palisades)

# safety 1 – any data at all?
if fire.size().getInfo() == 0:
    print('No fire imagery for Jan 2025.')
    print('C1')
    exit()

# 3. cumulative burned area snapshots
pre6  = fire.filterDate('2025-01-01','2025-01-06')
thru14= fire.filterDate('2025-01-01','2025-01-15')

def burnedPixels(col,name):
    if col.size().getInfo()==0:
        print(f'{name}: No images'); return 0
    comp = col.select('BurnDate').toBands()
    mask = comp.gt(0)    # 0 means unburned
    count = mask.selfMask().reduceRegion(
               reducer=ee.Reducer.count(),
               geometry=palisades, scale=1000, maxPixels=1e9).values().getInfo()
    return sum(count) if count else 0

burn6  = burnedPixels(pre6,'pre6')
burn14 = burnedPixels(thru14,'thru14')

# safety 2 – no valid pixels
if burn6+burn14==0:
    print('No valid burn pixels.')
    print('C2')
    exit()

print(f'Burned pixels total: before6={burn6}  through14={burn14}')
if burn14 > burn6:
    print('A')
else:
    print('B')
